title: Does one evidence root correspond to one underlying observation?
frozenBefore: any corpus item was selected, any identity was computed, and any label was assigned under this rule
whyFrozenFirst: The quantity under test is a ratio between two counts, one of which (labelled observations) is produced by human judgement. A labelling rule written after seeing the root identities is a rule chosen knowing what ratio it produces. Freezing first, and blinding labellers to the identities, is the only thing separating this from an exercise that returns whatever number is wanted.

question.plain: When five issuers report the same event, does the aggregator see one root or five?
question.formal: For each proposition p, let R(p) be the number of distinct mp-root-v1 identities among parentless claims asserting p, and O(p) the number of distinct underlying observations those claims rest on, established by blinded labelling. Estimate the distribution of R(p)/O(p).
question.whyNotAnswerable: No theorem settles this. Every theorem in formal/lean/ is correct GIVEN the identity criterion; the criterion is an input, not a conclusion. mp-root-v1 (provenance/ROOT-IDENTITY.md) makes identity unforgeable, which is a different property from making it correspond to an observation. Issuer is part of the digest, so two issuers reporting one event produce two identities by construction.

population.frame: published claims about factual propositions that have since resolved, where each claim carries an authenticated issuer, a proposition identifier, an asserted value and an evidence reference sufficient to compute mp-root-v1
population.selection: the frame, the source set and the proposition list are declared at collection start and recorded in the manifest; neither is extended, narrowed or re-sampled after any identity is computed or any label is assigned
population.why: Below three claims a proposition cannot exhibit a split. Two hundred propositions is the smallest frame that can distinguish a median split factor of 1.0 from 1.5 at the spread seen in constructed cases; it is registered here rather than chosen later from the observed variance.
exclusions: propositions whose claims all originate from one issuer -- no split is possible and they only dilute the estimate
claims whose evidence reference is absent, since mp-root-v1 is not computable and the item is neither a split nor a merge but a missing input
population.exclusionsAreDeclaredNotDiscovered: both exclusions are properties of the record, decidable before any label exists

identityArm.definition: SHA-256 over authenticated issuer, issuer-scoped observation identifier, proposition, asserted value and evidence digest, per provenance/ROOT-IDENTITY.md
identityArm.computedBy: the shipped implementation, not a reimplementation, so the number measured is the number the system would act on
identityArm.blinding: identities are computed and sealed before labelling begins and are not visible to labellers

observationArm.unit: an underlying observation event -- the act of witnessing, not the act of reporting
observationArm.rule: two claims rest on the same observation if a labeller, seeing only the claim texts, their cited sources and their timestamps, judges that neither could have been produced without the other's source or a common source they both cite
observationArm.independence: labellers work independently, do not see each other's labels, and do not see any mp-root-v1 identity, issuer digest or root count

interRaterThreshold.statistic: Krippendorff alpha on the same-observation partition
interRaterThreshold.why: Below this the partition is not reproducible and the denominator of the ratio is noise. 0.67 is the conventional floor for tentative conclusions and is registered now so it cannot be relaxed to rescue a run.
interRaterThreshold.onFailure: the run STOPS and reports that the ground truth was not establishable on this corpus. It is not retried on a different corpus chosen because it agrees better; a second corpus, if any, is a new registration.

observationArm.adjudication: disagreements are resolved by majority of the three labellers; items with no majority are reported as unresolved and counted in a declared sensitivity band, not silently dropped

endpoint.primary: median split factor, median over propositions of R(p)/O(p)
endpoint.H0: median split factor = 1.0 -- root identity tracks observation identity
secondary: merge rate: proportion of labelled observation pairs judged distinct that share one mp-root-v1 identity
split factor distribution, not only its median, since a long tail matters even at a benign median
endpoint.bothDirectionsMatter: Split inflates margin and overstates security. Merge destroys margin and causes false abstention. They are different failures with different owners and are reported separately, never netted.

effectRequires.property: the measure can detect a split at all
effectRequires.rule: on constructed cases where the number of underlying observations is known by construction, the computed split factor must recover the constructed value exactly
effectRequires.why: If mp-root-v1 collapsed everything to one identity, the real run would return 1.0 for a reason that has nothing to do with reporting behaviour. This is a sensitivity check on the instrument, run before the corpus, and it is not a result.
effectRequires.onFailure: the instrument is wrong and the real run does not start

effectRequires.property: the corpus can exhibit a split
effectRequires.rule: at least 20% of propositions must carry claims from three or more distinct issuers
effectRequires.why: A corpus where issuers rarely overlap cannot distinguish the hypotheses, however sound the method. Registered as a precondition rather than discovered as an excuse.

stopRule: collection ends at the declared proposition list, at the inter-rater failure condition, or at the instrument-sensitivity failure, whichever is first. The list is not extended and the labelling rule is not amended to obtain a result.

decisionRule.ifMedianSplitFactorAtOrBelow1_2: flip_budget may be described as an operational security budget, with the measured factor and its confidence interval disclosed alongside.
decisionRule.ifMedianSplitFactorAbove1_2: flip_budget must not be published as an operational security budget without dividing by the measured factor and disclosing the divisor. formal/CLAIM-SCOPE.md and PROVENANCE-REQUIREMENTS.md R3 are amended in the same change.
decisionRule.ifRunStops: the first gate in HRI-1 stands unchanged: flip_budget remains publishable as a count of root-set units, which is what it provably is, and not as a security budget.
decisionRule.why: The consequence is registered before the number exists so that an inconvenient result cannot be re-described as a limitation of the corpus.

whatThisDoesNotMeasure: whether any observation is true -- this is an independence measure, not an accuracy measure
deliberate identity splitting by one controller, which is HVI-1's question and has a different remedy
whether a production deployment uses RootRegistry at all, which is a deployment property recorded as LEDGER-H2 deployment_status
priorWork: None. This quantity has not been measured. formal/EXTENSION-SOCKETS.md section 5 identified it as the socket where a measurement, not a theorem, is what is missing; formal/THEOREM-LEDGER.json carries it as U1 underspecified.
amendedBefore: any query was issued under this rule
whyAmended: v0.3's arm A was not assemblable, for a reason that outranks the arm: a coordinated replication publishes ~125 independent observations as ONE work, so the citation graph sees one node. That was the third time a registered assumption about the artifact-to-claim mapping failed (v0.1: no evidence digest exists; v0.2: 56% cite no primary source; v0.3: observations arrive bundled). The common cause is that the formalism has no defined UNIT. v0.4 stops measuring the split factor and measures the prerequisite instead.

evidenceDigestConstruction.why: mp-root-v1 digests an evidence_digest that real published claims do not carry. How it is constructed is the single most consequential free parameter in this measurement and is pinned here, before any retrieval.

rules.rule: sha256 of the claim's own published text, normalised to lowercase with runs of whitespace collapsed
rules.models: a deployment in which each issuer digests the artefact it produced
rules.expectedDirection: maximal split: every issuer distinct by construction, so the split factor equals the number of issuers per observation

rules.rule: sha256 of the identifier of the primary source the claim cites -- wire slug, dataset DOI, filing number, court docket, official release URL. A claim citing no primary source falls back to D1 for that claim only, and the fallback count is reported.
rules.models: a deployment in which each issuer digests the underlying evidence rather than its own retelling
rules.expectedDirection: minimal split: claims resting on one primary source collapse to one root

evidenceDigestConstruction.primaryReported: both, side by side, never one alone
evidenceDigestConstruction.theRatioIsTheFinding: D1 split divided by D2 split quantifies how much the whole measurement depends on a choice that provenance/ROOT-IDENTITY.md does not currently constrain. If that ratio is near 1 the choice does not matter and the parameter is benign. If it is large, mp-root-v1 does not have a determinate split factor at all until the deployment fixes the digest convention -- which would be a finding about the SPECIFICATION, not about reporting behaviour.
evidenceDigestConstruction.notPinnedAndWhy: A transitive first-mover rule (resolve citation chains to the earliest publisher) is a plausible third construction and is deliberately OUT of scope for the pilot: it requires a citation graph the pilot corpus will not reliably support, and adding an under-supported third arm would widen the reported range without evidence.

pilotArm.whyExploratory: Labelling of 'same underlying observation' will be performed by one agent under one operator. Per AGENTS.md boundaries 2 and 3 that is a single control domain: internal replication, not the three independent blinded labellers the confirmatory design requires. Its inter-rater statistic is therefore undefined, not merely unmeasured.
pilotArm.whatItCanEstablish: feasibility, the order of magnitude of the D1/D2 ratio, and whether the confirmatory run is worth human labelling time
pilotArm.whatItCannotEstablish: any answer to HRI-1, in either direction
pilotArm.mustBeLabelled: every artefact and every number carries 'exploratory pilot, one control domain, not a result'
pilotArm.size: 3 to 6 resolved propositions, at least 4 claims each; declared before retrieval and not extended

replicationArm.why: In a multi-lab registered replication, N laboratories independently execute one protocol. O(p)=N is established by the study design, before this experiment existed, by people unconnected to it. No labelling, no judgement, no control-domain problem. This is the strongest ground truth available to HRI-1 and the only one that makes a confirmatory run executable without three blinded human labellers.
replicationArm.theDecisiveProperty: Every replicating lab cites the SAME original protocol paper while producing a GENUINELY INDEPENDENT observation. Citation lineage and evidence independence therefore point in opposite directions, and the study design says which one is right. This is the sharpest available test of whether a reference-based root criterion measures independence or merely measures citation.
replicationArm.exposesAGapInTheModel: Shared method is not shared observation. Twenty labs running one protocol share HOW they looked, not WHAT they saw. World in formal/lean/ has one edge type and cannot express the distinction. If this arm shows the criteria failing here, the deficiency is in the model, not in the data.

subCorpora.frame: multi-lab registered replication reports and coordinated many-lab projects, where the number of independently executing sites is stated in the report
subCorpora.groundTruth: O(p) = number of independently executing sites, taken verbatim from the report

subCorpora.frame: multiple works reanalysing one named public dataset or cohort, where reuse is stated
subCorpora.groundTruth: O(p) = 1: one underlying observation, many analyses
subCorpora.why: Arm A alone can be passed by a criterion that never merges anything. Arm B is the counter-test that such a criterion must fail. A criterion is only sound if it passes BOTH.

rootCriteria.rule: two claims share an evidence root if their reference sets intersect at all
rootCriteria.expectedDirection: over-merges: replicating labs all cite the protocol paper, so arm A collapses toward 1 against a truth of N

rootCriteria.rule: two claims share an evidence root only if one directly cites the other
rootCriteria.expectedDirection: under-merges: replicating labs do not cite each other, so arm A gives N; but arm B's independent reanalyses of one dataset also do not cite each other, so it gives many against a truth of 1

replicationArm.theRealEndpoint: whether ANY single reference-based criterion recovers the truth in BOTH arms. The registered expectation is that neither does: R1 fails arm A, R2 fails arm B. If that holds, the finding is that citation structure does not determine evidence independence, and mp-root-v1 cannot be computed from a citation graph without an evidence-edge criterion that the specification does not currently define -- the same class of gap as the digest convention in v0.2, found in a second place.
replicationArm.whatWouldRefuteThat: either criterion recovering the truth in both arms, which would make citation structure a usable proxy for independence and would be a substantially more positive result than expected
replicationArm.noHumanLabelling: Ground truth in both arms is read from study metadata, not judged. The control-domain objection that blocks the news arm does not apply. This arm is therefore CONFIRMATORY-CAPABLE, unlike the pilot.
replicationArm.stopRule: the sub-corpora are declared before any query and are not extended. If fewer than the declared minimum qualify, the shortfall is reported and no estimate is given.
replicationArm.supersededBy: v0.4 unitOfClaim; arm A remains unassemblable until a unit rule exists, and this is recorded rather than removed

unitOfClaim.problem: formal/lean/ defines World = (parents, assert) over claims indexed by Fin n, and proves everything about that. Nothing anywhere states what ONE CLAIM is when evidence arrives as a 125-sample coordinated replication, an unattributed news item, or a reanalysis of someone else's cohort. The artifact-to-claim mapping is many-to-many and undefined, so every downstream count -- roots, margin, flip_budget -- is defined only up to a choice nobody has made.
unitOfClaim.relationToU1: Ledger U1 asks when two roots are the same root. This is prior to it: what is one claim. A root identity criterion cannot be evaluated until the things being identified are defined. Recommend registering as U4 in formal/THEOREM-LEDGER.json once PR #79 lands; not edited here to avoid conflicting with that PR.

regimesFoundEmpirically.example: a report of an event the reporter witnessed
Many Labs 2: one OpenAlex record, ~125 independently collected samples
a meta-analysis, a review, a reanalysis of another group's cohort

candidateRules.registeredExpectation: fails G-bundled-independent (counts 1 against a truth of N) and fails G-bundled-derivative (counts 1 new root against a truth of 0). Simple, machine-derivable, and wrong in both bundled regimes.

candidateRules.rule: one independently executed observation is one claim
candidateRules.registeredExpectation: correct by definition and unimplementable from metadata. Requires reading the artifact, and 'independently executed' is precisely the judgement the ground-truth design exists to avoid. Registered so that its correctness is not mistaken for availability.

candidateRules.rule: one claim is whatever the artifact itself declares as a separable observation -- a sample, site, run, cohort or numbered experiment
candidateRules.registeredExpectation: recovers all three regimes, because coordinated replications do report per-site counts and meta-analyses do declare that their inputs are others' studies. Transcription, not judgement: the analyst reads a number the producer wrote.
candidateRules.theProblemWithIt: THE UNIT COUNT BECOMES PRODUCER-CONTROLLED. An issuer that wants to look like more evidence declares more units. This is the sybil problem one layer below where R1 addresses it.

candidateRules.rule: mint no root for an artifact whose unit structure is not machine-determinable
candidateRules.registeredExpectation: sound in all three regimes by declining the ambiguous ones. Cost is coverage, and the pilot suggests the cost is severe: 56% of news claims could not identify their evidence and would be refused.

securityConsequenceRegisteredNow.finding: If the unit is producer-declared (U-C), R1.4 currently bounds the wrong quantity. R1.4 caps roots per authenticated issuer per window. An issuer inside its quota can still inflate its evidential mass by declaring more units inside one artifact, because the quota counts issuance events rather than observation units.
securityConsequenceRegisteredNow.correction: R1.4's quota must be denominated in declared observation units, not in artifacts or issuance requests.
securityConsequenceRegisteredNow.whyRegisteredHere: It is a consequence of the unit rule, so it is stated before the rule is chosen rather than discovered after one is adopted.
securityConsequenceRegisteredNow.status: hypothesis about the requirement stack, not a measured result

endpoint.primary: regime distribution: for a declared corpus, the proportion of artifacts in each of G-atomic, G-bundled-independent and G-bundled-derivative
endpoint.why: It settles how much the unit gap matters. If real corpora are overwhelmingly G-atomic, U-A is an acceptable approximation and the gap is theoretical. If bundled regimes are common, no downstream count means anything until the unit rule is fixed.
endpoint.secondary: for each candidate rule, which regimes it recovers -- a 4x3 table, reported whole, never a selected row
endpoint.H0: the regime distribution is overwhelmingly G-atomic and the unit gap is theoretical

unitOfClaim.registeredExpectationOverall: No single rule is both sound and safe. U-A is safe and wrong; U-B is right and unimplementable; U-C is right and attacker-controlled; U-D is safe and low-coverage. The anticipated resolution is a combination -- U-C for the unit, a quota denominated in units, U-D as the fallback for artifacts that declare nothing -- and stating that expectation now means a result matching it is confirmation rather than discovery.
unitOfClaim.whatWouldRefuteThat: any single rule recovering all three regimes without introducing a producer-controlled quantity, which would make the unit gap closable by definition alone
unitOfClaim.stopRule: corpus declared before any query and not extended; regimes assigned from the artifact's own declarations, and artifacts whose regime cannot be assigned from their declarations are reported as unassignable rather than defaulted to G-atomic.
